content:
We need to identify elements based on isotope distribution patterns visible in the mass spectrum. We need the mass spectrum data. Use mass_spectrometry_spectra tool to get spectrum. Then analyze isotopic patterns to identify elements that can be definitively identified. We also have retrieve_isotope_distribution to get isotopic patterns for elements.

We need to look at the spectrum string. Then see peaks that correspond to characteristic isotopic patterns: e.g., chlorine (Cl-35, Cl-37 ~ 3:1 ratio, 2 Da apart), bromine (Br-79, Br-81 ~ 1:1 ratio, 2 Da apart), sulfur (S-32, S-34 ~ 4:1 ratio, 2 Da apart), carbon (C-13 ~ 1.1% of C-12, small M+1), nitrogen (N-15 ~0.37% M+1), oxygen (O-18 ~0.2% M+2). But "definitively identified" likely means clear patterns like Cl, Br, S, maybe isotopic peaks for C (M+1) but that's subtle. Usually you can definitively identify Cl, Br, S based on distinct patterns. Also maybe I (I-127 only). But isotopic distribution patterns visible: we need to see the spectrum.

Let's call mass_spectrometry_spectra.
